paper.title: Dominate or Delete: Decentralized Competing Bandits in Serial Dictatorship

unmapped: two-sided matching market: N ranked agents, K >= N arms; arm matches highest-ranked proposing agent, others blocked (asymmetric collisions) and notified, receiving 0
heterogeneous agent-specific arm means, all distinct per agent
regret per agent measured against the unique stable matching partner arm
decentralized: each agent only uses own observations; agents do not know their rank a priori
settings.definition_quote: An agent is \emph{matched} to the arm of its choice in a given round, if and only if it is the highest ranked agent playing that arm at that time. Otherwise, it is \emph{blocked}. If agent $j \in [N]$ is matched with arm $k \in [K]$ at any time, then, agent $j$ is receives a stochastic $[0,1]$ valued reward with mean $\mu_{jk} \in (0,1)$ ... The regret of any agent $j \in [N]$, after $T$ time steps is ${R}_T^{(j)} = \sum_{t=1}^T  \mathbb{E} [\mu_{jk^{(j)}_*} - \mu_{j I^{(j)}(t)} \mathbf{1}_{{M_{I^{(j)}(t)}(t)} = j}].$

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized serial dictatorship, Optimally Stable Bandits (lower bound)
unmapped: two-sided matching market with serial-dictatorship blocking (highest-ranked proposer wins arm)
instances restricted to Optimally Stable Bandits: each agent's stable match is its overall best arm
regret per agent against the stable matching
settings.definition_quote: Let us consider the class of bandit instances where dominated arms are bad, i.e. for any instance $\boldsymbol{\nu}$ in this class, for all agents $j \in [N]$,  $\mu_{jk} < \mu_{jk_*^{(j)}}$ for all arms $k \in [K]\setminus \{k^{(j)}_*\}$ . We call this class of instances Optimally Stable Bandits (OSB)

symbols.Reg_coll: sum_{j'<j} sum_{k in A*_j} (9 alpha log T/(Delta^{(j')}_k)^2 + 1 + 178 T^{-4alpha}/(Delta^{(j')}_k)^2 + T^{2-4alpha}) mu_{j k*_j}
symbols.Reg_sub: sum_{k in A*_j minus k*_j} (9 alpha log T/(Delta^{(j)}_k)^2 + 1 + 178 T^{-4alpha}/(Delta^{(j)}_k)^2 + T^{2-4alpha}) Delta^{(j)}_k
symbols.i_star: min{i in N: 20 N K alpha i/Delta^2 <= 2^{i-1}}, Delta the smallest non-dominated gap across agents

conditions: arm means of each agent are distinct and in (0,1)

source.label: thm:main_thm_algo
source.quote: Suppose every agent runs \name\; with $\alpha \geq 2$, then the regret of any agent with rank $j$ satisfies \mathbb{E}[R_T^{(j)}] \leq 2(j-1)(\log_2(T)+1) + ... +N + j(2^{i^*}+i^* + 4(NK)^2 + 3NK) + \frac{2NK}{T^{2\alpha-4}}, where $i^* {:=} \min \left\{ i {\in} \mathbb{N}: \tfrac{20 NK \alpha i }{\Delta^2} \leq 2^{i-1} \right\}.

results.notes: Per-agent regret relative to the stable-match partner arm (comparator not in vocabulary). Collision and sub-optimal sums declared as symbols. Regret is through means (pseudo-regret).

conditions: Delta_min here is the smallest gap of non-dominated arms across all agents

source.label: cor:UBcor
source.quote: Suppose every agent runs \name\; with parameter $\alpha \geq  2$, then the regret of any agent with rank $j$ after $T$ time steps satisfies \mathbb{E}[R_T^{(j)}] \leq 9\alpha \log(T) \left(  \tfrac{(j-1)(K+1-j)}{\Delta^2} + \tfrac{[K-1-j]_{+}}{\Delta}\right) + O \left( (NK)^2 + \tfrac{NK}{\Delta^2}\log \left(\tfrac{NK}{\Delta^2} \right) \right)

results.notes: Leading log(T) term has explicit constant; additive term is O(.). Recorded whole as O.

symbols.LB_coll: sum_{j'<j} Delta^{(j)}_min / D_inf(nu_{j' k*_j}, mu_{j' k*_{j'}}, P)
symbols.LB_sub: sum over arms k (as indexed in the paper) of Delta^{(j)}_k / D_inf(nu_{jk}, mu_{j k*_j}, P)

conditions: OSB instance (each agent's stable match is its optimal arm)

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: For any agent $j\in [N]$, under any decentralized universally consistent algorithm $\pi$  on a OSB instance $\boldsymbol{\nu}$ satisfies \liminf\limits_{T\to \infty} \frac{R_T^{(j)}(\boldsymbol{\nu}, \pi)}{\log T} \geq \max\{ ... \}

results.notes: Second sum's index set as written is odd (k notin A_j minus k*); recorded via declared symbol. D_inf is a K_inf-type quantity over [0,1]-supported distributions.

conditions: exists an OSB instance with Bernoulli rewards (existential lower bound)

source.label: corr:simple
source.quote: There exists a OSB bandit instance with Bernoulli rewards, where the regert of agent $j$ is lower bounded as $\Omega\left(\max\left\{\tfrac{(j-1)\log T}{\Delta^2}, \tfrac{K\log T}{\Delta}\right\}\right)$.

results.notes: Follows from asymptotic Theorem 7; proof gives (j-1)log(T)/(16 Delta^2). Delta is the gap of higher-ranked agents in the construction.
